TASK: Report exactly what `consolidateDuplicateBonusProducts` does to a list of basket ProductItems:
1. Which items does it merge, and on what key?
2. When it merges two items, EXACTLY which numeric fields does it sum / recompute / carry over unchanged? Specifically: `quantity`, `price`, `basePrice`, `priceAfterItemDiscount`, `priceAfterOrderDiscount`, `pricePerUnit`, `adjustedTax`, `tax`, `taxBasis`. Quote the actual code.

This establishes the house convention. Include node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/ in the grep too.

Also grep for any place that computes a per-unit price by dividing (e.g. `/ quantity`, `/item.quantity`) — I want to know if dividing is an established pattern anywhere or if this PR is the first.

Cite file:line for everything. Quote actual code for the merge logic.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

80	/**
81	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
82	 * pricing, taking into account applied discounts as well as base item prices.
83	 */
84	const ItemPrice = ({ currency, align = 'right', baseDirection = 'column', ...props }: ItemPriceProps) => {
85	  const variant: SfccVariant = useItemVariant();
86	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE, {});
87	  const { price, priceAfterItemDiscount, quantity } = variant;
88	  const isASet = variant?.type?.set;
89	  const isMaster = variant?.type?.master;
90	  let priceData;
91	  // When variant has basket pricing, we should prioritize these prices for displaying
92	  // since they may have take promotion/discount into account
93	  // NOTE: try NOT to re-calculate these values since basket-level discount is complicated
94	  if (variant?.itemId) {
95	    // 1:1 Figma-alignment audit fix, 2026-09-22 (Marcel's direct report, confirmed once
96	    // Gideon's backend bypass made real pricing visible): SFCC's basket `price`/
97	    // `priceAfterItemDiscount` are the LINE TOTAL, already multiplied by quantity — not a
98	    // per-unit value. Confirmed two ways: commerce-sdk-isomorphic's own generated doc comment on
99	    // `basePrice` ("the unit price... not including adjustments", a distinct field), and directly
100	    // against a live basket (qty 1 -> 3 on the same line: basePrice stayed flat, price/
101	    // priceAfterItemDiscount scaled 1200 -> 3600). Figma's own Cart Item spec shows a flat
102	    // per-unit price regardless of quantity (CART MERGE state, node 9323:65962 — a quantity-3
103	    // line shows the identical $825 as the quantity-1 lines beside it). `DisplayPrice` below
104	    // already does its own `currentPrice * quantity` multiplication for a caller that wants a
105	    // total (see the wishlist branch below, which passes `quantity` explicitly for exactly that
106	    // reason) — so passing it SFCC's own already-multiplied line total double-counts in the
107	    // wrong direction. Dividing back down to a genuine per-unit value here, and deliberately NOT
108	    // passing a `quantity` prop below (defaults to 1, a no-op), is what makes the two mechanisms
109	    // agree instead of compound. `|| 1` guards a variant with no real quantity yet rather than
110	    // dividing by zero — a real basket line always has quantity >= 1, so this is a fallback for a
111	    // shape SFCC would never actually send, not an expected runtime path.
112	    const unitQuantity = quantity || 1;
113	    priceData = {
114	      currentPrice: priceAfterItemDiscount / unitQuantity,
115	      // we don't want to show strikethrough price for cart since listPrice is not available via basket pricing
116	      listPrice: null,
117	      isASet,
118	      isMaster,
119	      isRange: isASet || isMaster || false,
120	      isOnSale: price > priceAfterItemDiscount,
121	    };
122	  } else {
123	    // for wishlist page we extract price info from variant/product obj
124	    priceData = getPriceData(variant);
125	  }
126	
127	  return (
128	    <Stack
129	      sx={styles.price}
130	      textAlign={align}
131	      direction={baseDirection}
132	      justifyContent={align === 'left' ? 'flex-start' : 'flex-end'}
133	      alignItems="baseline"
134	      spacing={priceData?.isOnSale ? 0 : 1}
135	      wrap="nowrap"
136	      {...props}
137	    >
138	      {variant?.itemId ? (
139	        <DisplayPrice
140	          labelForA11y={variant?.name}
141	          currency={currency}
142	          priceData={priceData}
143	          listPriceProps={{ fontSize: 'sm' }}
144	          currentPriceProps={{ fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)' }}
145	        />
146	      ) : (
147	        <DisplayPrice
148	          labelForA11y={variant?.name}
149	          currency={currency}
150	          priceData={priceData}
151	          quantity={variant?.quantity}
152	          listPriceProps={{ fontSize: 'sm' }}
153	          currentPriceProps={{ fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)' }}
154	        />
155	      )}
156	    </Stack>
157	  );
158	};

content.text:
## 1. Location

`consolidateDuplicateBonusProducts` is at **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/bonus-product/cart.js:564`** (path as you gave it — correct).

The actual merge is **not** in that function. It delegates to a private helper, `aggregateBonusProductQuantities`, at **`cart.js:78`**. That is where all the field handling lives.

## 2. What it merges, and on what key

`cart.js:573-586`:

```js
    productItems.forEach((item) => {
        if (item.bonusProductLineItem) {
            bonusProducts.push(item)
        } else {
            regularProducts.push(item)
        }
    })

    // Consolidate duplicate bonus products by productId
    const consolidatedBonusProducts = aggregateBonusProductQuantities(bonusProducts)

    // Combine regular products with consolidated bonus products
    // Keep regular products first, then bonus products
    return [...regularProducts, ...consolidatedBonusProducts]
```

- Only items with truthy `item.bonusProductLineItem` are candidates. Regular lines pass through byte-identical and are **reordered to the front**.
- Merge key is **`productId` alone**. Not `bonusDiscountLineItemId`, not `shipmentId`, not price, not `itemId`.

## 3. Exactly which numeric fields are summed / recomputed / carried over

The whole merge, `cart.js:78-98`:

```js
const aggregateBonusProductQuantities = (bonusItems) => {
    const productQuantityMap = new Map()

    bonusItems.forEach((item) => {
        const existingQuantity = productQuantityMap.get(item.productId) || 0
        productQuantityMap.set(item.productId, existingQuantity + (item.quantity || 0))
    })

    const result = []
    productQuantityMap.forEach((quantity, productId) => {
        const sampleItem = bonusItems.find((item) => item.productId === productId)
        if (sampleItem) {
            result.push({
                ...sampleItem,
                quantity: quantity
            })
        }
    })

    return result
}
```

`sampleItem` is `bonusItems.find(...)` — the **first** bonus line with that `productId`. The merged object is that first line spread wholesale, with exactly one key overwritten.

| Field | Treatment |
|---|---|
| `quantity` | **Summed** (`cart.js:83`), `\|\| 0` guard for missing |
| `price` | **Carried over unchanged from the first line.** Not summed, not recomputed |
| `basePrice` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `priceAfterItemDiscount` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `priceAfterOrderDiscount` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `pricePerUnit` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `adjustedTax` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `tax` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `taxBasis` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |

Nothing is summed except `quantity`. Nothing is recomputed. There is no field-specific logic at all — the spread is blind, so any field you name that isn't `quantity` is first-line-wins.

## 4. Is the merged `price` coherent with the merged `quantity`?

**No.** `quantity` becomes `Σ qᵢ` while `price` stays `line₀.price` (which, per the house convention below, is line₀'s *line total*, i.e. `unit × q₀`). So on a merged item:

```
price / quantity  ==  (unit × q₀) / Σqᵢ     ≠  unit
```

Two bonus lines of qty 1 at unit 100 merge to `{quantity: 2, price: 100}` → `price/quantity = 50`. Under-reports by a factor of N for N equal-quantity lines.

**Severity caveat worth knowing before you act on this:** the canonical SFCC bonus line shape is all-zeros on money. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/mocks/mock-data.js:5739-5757` — `adjustedTax: 0, basePrice: 0, price: 0, priceAfterItemDiscount: 0, priceAfterOrderDiscount: 0, tax: 0, taxBasis: 0`, and **`pricePerUnit` is absent entirely**. For a 100%-off bonus, `0 / anything === 0`, so the incoherence is latent. It becomes a real wrong number only for a partially-discounted bonus product (percentage-off "choice of bonus"), where `price` is nonzero.

The upstream tests do not constrain this at all: across the entire describe block (`cart.test.js:1643-1990`) the string `price` appears **zero** times. No fixture even has a price field. So there is no upstream contract you'd be breaking by changing the behaviour, and no upstream test that would catch a regression.

## 5. `itemId` and `bonusDiscountLineItemId`

- **`itemId`**: preserved, from the **first line only**. Not regenerated, not cleared. The merged object claims line₀'s `itemId` while carrying the summed quantity of N lines — so it is no longer a valid handle for a quantity-update or remove mutation. Upstream documents this deliberately: `cart.test.js:1966` — `test('itemId is not used in consolidation logic (only for display keys)')`, asserting at :1990 `expect(result[0].quantity).toBe(3) // Consolidated despite different itemIds`. Both call sites treat it as a React key only (`order-summary/index.jsx:88`, `order-detail.jsx:79` uses `index`).
- **`bonusDiscountLineItemId`**: preserved from the **first line only** — all other merged lines' IDs are **silently dropped**. `cart.test.js:1817` asserts `expect(result[0].bonusDiscountLineItemId).toBe('bonus-123')` but only in a case where both merged lines already had `'bonus-123'`. The test at `cart.test.js:1682-1713` merges `'bonus-123'`, `'bonus-123'` and `'bonus-456'` into one item and **never asserts the resulting `bonusDiscountLineItemId`** — the `'bonus-456'` loss is real and untested.

---

## House convention: every real read of these fields

### `price` / `priceAfterItemDiscount` → LINE TOTAL

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price.jsx:43,52,59`** — base reads `{price, priceAfterItemDiscount}`, assigns `currentPrice: priceAfterItemDiscount`, and at `:139-144` passes it to `DisplayPrice` with **no `quantity` prop**. Implies line total: base wants the already-multiplied number rendered as-is.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/index.jsx:35,43,56`** — `quantity = 1` default, then `price={currentPrice * quantity}` and `price={listPrice * quantity}`. Implies `DisplayPrice`'s own contract is **unit price in, caller opts into multiplication**. This is the crux of the mismatch: base feeds it a line total and relies on the `quantity=1` default to make the double-count a no-op.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-shipping-options.jsx:316`** — `shippingItem?.priceAfterItemDiscount || 0`. No signal: a shipping item is always quantity 1.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/partials/pickup-address.jsx:393`** — PropTypes declaration only, no read.

### `pricePerUnit` → UNIT price (base's own admission)

- **`item-price.jsx:55`** — `pricePerUnit: variant?.pricePerUnit` into `priceData`.
- **`item-price.jsx:77-78` and `:98-99`** — `{!isDesktop && variant?.quantity > 1 && !isASet && priceData?.pricePerUnit && (<PricePerItem currency={currency} basePrice={priceData.pricePerUnit} />)}`. Gated on **`quantity > 1`**. This is upstream stating outright that the main price element is *not* per-unit — otherwise a separate "ea" element gated on quantity > 1 would be redundant.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:158`** — `pricePerUnit: product?.pricePerUnit` in `getPriceData`, the wishlist/PDP (non-basket) path.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/index.jsx:84`** — PropTypes only.

### `basePrice` → UNIT price (authoritative)

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:6914`** (in the doc block for the `ProductItem` type declared at `:6968`): *"basePrice: The base price of the line item, which is the unit price not including adjustments."* This is the ground truth your `item-price.tsx:99` comment cites, and it checks out verbatim.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/multiship/multiship-order-summary.jsx:60`** — `price: pli.price || pli.basePrice || pli.itemTotal || undefined`. **Incoherent upstream bug**, useful as evidence: it treats a line total (`price`), a unit price (`basePrice`) and a line total (`itemTotal`) as interchangeable fallbacks for one display slot. Base is not internally consistent here, so don't treat base as a reliable convention authority.
- **`item-price.jsx:19,22,34`** — `PricePerItem`'s prop is *named* `basePrice` but is always fed `pricePerUnit`, never the actual `basePrice` field. Naming noise only.

### `priceAfterOrderDiscount` → read NOWHERE

Zero reads in `overrides/` or `retail-react-app/app/`. Every hit is a generated type declaration: `commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperBaskets/helpers.d.ts:83,148` and `commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperBasketsV2/helpers.d.ts:91,167,232,342,418,483,559,624`. No convention is established by usage — if you need it, you're the first.

---

## Division to get a per-unit price: this PR is the first

Single hit across `overrides/`, `retail-react-app/app/` and `commerce-sdk-react/`:

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-price.tsx:114`** — `currentPrice: priceAfterItemDiscount / unitQuantity`, with `const unitQuantity = quantity || 1;` at `:112`. Introduced by commit **98b0d609** `fix(cart): SFCC-11 cart item price shows the per-unit price, not price × quantity`.

Nearest other divisions, both unrelated to price:
- `retail-react-app/app/utils/bonus-product/cart.js:261` — `(totalPromotionCapacity / totalQualifyingQuantity) * (qualifyingItem.quantity || 1)`, promotion capacity allocation.
- `retail-react-app/app/components/product-view-modal/bundle.jsx:133` — `const quantityPerBundle = product.quantity / bundle.quantity`, quantity-per-bundle, not money.

So: dividing a money field by `quantity` is **not** an established pattern. This PR is the first instance.

---

## The collision you should care about

Your overridden `ItemPrice` is rendered from more than the cart drawer, and the two paths disagree on whether it receives a raw or consolidated line:

- **Cart drawer (safe)** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx:426` takes `basket?.productItems ?? []` and `:267` maps them straight into `ProductItem`. **No consolidation.** The divide at `item-price.tsx:114` sees a genuine basket line, so `price/quantity` is correct.
- **Order summary (broken)** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/order-summary/index.jsx:77-80` calls `consolidateDuplicateBonusProducts(basket.productItems || [])`, then at `:82-86` builds `variant = {...product, ...products[product.productId], price: product.price}` and hands it to `ItemVariantProvider` → `CartItemVariantPrice` → your override. Here `quantity` is the sum but `priceAfterItemDiscount` is line₀'s. `OrderSummary` is rendered by base `pages/cart/index.jsx`, `pages/checkout/index.jsx`, `pages/checkout-one-click/index.jsx` and `pages/account/order-detail.jsx`.
- **Order detail (broken)** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/account/order-detail.jsx:62-63`, same consolidation, same `ItemVariantProvider` feed at `:82`.

Scope of the breakage is narrow: bonus lines only, and only bonus lines that are duplicated by `productId` **and** carry nonzero money (a partially-discounted bonus). A fully-free bonus divides 0 by N and renders 0 either way. Note also that base's old `PricePerItem` never fired on bonus lines regardless, because the canonical bonus shape has no `pricePerUnit` field at all and the guard at `item-price.jsx:77` is truthiness on `priceData?.pricePerUnit` — so removing it cost nothing on this path.
